patients.summary: Elementary school teacher who joined the practice healthy in 2018, developed immune thrombocytopenic purpura in 2021 managed by hematology on prednisone 10 mg with an ED visit and an IVIG admission for bleeding, then had right Bell palsy in 2023 (recurring in 2026) and vestibular neuritis in 2024.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
39 y/o woman, 3rd grade teacher in town, new to us. Her old primary care office was on the other side of the valley and she wanted something closer to school. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No chronic problems, no hospitalizations.
PSH: T&A at about 12, wisdom teeth out at 20. No problems with bleeding after either that she recalls.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: mother with an underactive thyroid, father with high blood pressure. Nobody in the family with a bleeding problem.
Social: never smoker. Wine at a dinner out maybe once or twice a month. Single, lives alone. Walks most evenings.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap about 3 years ago, normal per her.

ROS negative across the board.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal, TMs clear, oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash or bruising. No edema. Breast exam without masses. Pelvic deferred to the cervical sample only, collected without difficulty.

A/P
1. Health maintenance. Baseline labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH (given mom's thyroid). One-time hep C and HIV screen, she agrees. Pap with HPV co-test collected. Tdap today, last one she can't remember.
2. Mammogram: talked about starting at 40, she'd like to start next year.
3. Will request records from her prior office.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Amy, your blood work from Tuesday all came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and thyroid. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. The Pap result usually takes another week, I will send it when it's in.

reports.text: Specimen: liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV DNA: not detected.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test were both normal. With a normal co-test the next one is due in 5 years, so 2023.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records received from patient's previous primary care office, 2009 to 2017. Annual visits, no chronic diagnoses, no medications. Pap 2015 negative. Routine labs 2016 within normal limits. Immunization record shows a childhood series and a tetanus booster in 2006. Filed to chart; PCP reviewed, nothing to act on.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for her flu vaccine. Afebrile, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past. Given L deltoid, tolerated well. VIS provided.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Turned 40 last month. Busy spring with state testing at school but doing fine. No new symptoms. Not on any medicines.

ROS: no fatigue, weight change, chest pain, breathlessness, bowel or urinary change. Periods regular.
Family and social unchanged from last year.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Neck supple without thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft without masses or organomegaly. Skin clear. Breast exam normal bilaterally. No edema.

A/P: Healthy 40 y/o.
- Screening mammogram ordered, she will book it for after the school year gets quieter.
- CBC and BMP today. Lipids were fine last year, skip this year.
- Pap up to date (2023 next). Tdap 2018.
- Flu shot in the fall.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and chemistries from yesterday are all normal. Nothing to change.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies available for comparison. The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast. Axillae unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Routine annual screening recommended.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your first mammogram was normal. You'll get a letter from the breast center too. Repeat in a year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza vaccine given R deltoid. No issues with last year's dose. Tolerated, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to cancel her April physical; in-person preventive visits on hold during the COVID-19 shutdown. Offered a video check-in in June, she accepted.

events.reason: Video check-in in place of physical

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she's at her kitchen table, consented to a video visit. Finishing out the school year teaching remotely, which she says is exhausting in a different way than the classroom, but she's sleeping fine and mood is okay. Walking daily. No health concerns she wants to raise. No meds.

Appears well on camera, speaking full sentences, no distress.

Plan: hold the in-person physical and labs until things settle, probably the fall or next spring. Mammogram was due in May; she will call the breast center once they reopen screening. Flu shot in the fall. She'll reach out with anything in between.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2019. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, suspicious calcifications or architectural distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Mammogram report received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Screening mammogram 9/22 report received from breast imaging center, negative. Scanned; PCP reviewed.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Screened at door, no symptoms, afebrile. Masked. Flu vaccine L deltoid, tolerated well.
